A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ExPLoRA work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite reflow and added material.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification, segmentation, detection, ablation, and representation-analysis results in Sections 6–7 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and reports additional ablation outcomes, MAE comparisons on WILDS, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same block unfreezing, Q/V LoRA updates, normalization training, and MAE/DinoV2 objectives. Additional unfreezing configurations are evaluations within the existing method, not new algorithm components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same satellite datasets, three WILDS datasets, and VisDA2017, with the same task coverage. The new dataset summary in Table 18 and additional MAE results do not introduce new datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 7–8 add MAE with LoRA as a comparator on Camelyon17 and iWildcam. Table 3 adds a DinoV2 pre-training-from-scratch control. The extensive existing fMoW, PEFT, and VisDA comparison sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: Table 3 adds a 1200-GPU-hour from-scratch control and larger unfreezing configurations. v4 also reports hardware-standardized timing comparisons. New Table 18 gives some conflicting split counts: RESISC-45 has 18.9k training images there, versus 25.2k in Section 6.1.4 in both versions. Thus actual split changes or reruns cannot be established.

E4.justification: The block-selection study adds LoRA configurations unfreezing two and three blocks, plus a from-scratch control, extending the investigation of initialization and efficiency trade-offs. Existing decoder-rank, backbone-size, convergence, feature-probing, and attention-map analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained eigenvalue-variance analysis and attention-score filtering do not constitute uncertainty reporting for experimental performance.

E6.justification: v4 substantially expands computational results across the main tables and Table 16. Table 3 adds 54.29% accuracy for from-scratch pre-training and 77.76%/78.04% for larger unfreezing configurations. Tables 7–9 add MAE-related outcomes, including MAE-ExPLoRA scoring 79.3% versus MAE's 82.5% on GlobalWheat. Existing headline accuracies of 79.28% and 77.48% remain unchanged. Figure 7 also slightly lowers the 50k-pre-training endpoint.

T1.justification: The source/target assumptions, structured-update formulation, and Equations 1–6 retain their mathematical substance. Replacing the full-fine-tuning notation with an explicitly unrestricted parameter space is equivalent clarification; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal method and accuracy contributions are retained. The conclusion now explicitly claims 8–10 times less compute, extending the earlier introduction's claim of savings up to eightfold and strengthening the quantitative efficiency claim.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of amortizing pre-training costs, the preferred accuracy/efficiency trade-off, and MAE's lower computational cost. Appendix C.5 introduces broader guidance about limited data diversity and overfitting below 50k training samples. The iWildcam discussion changes its explanation from possible knowledge-transfer loss to possible overfitting.

D1.justification: Beyond v3's existing optimizer, architecture, and hardware details, v4 supplies extensive pre-training/fine-tuning timings and a dataset-wide table of split sizes and recommended iteration budgets. Appendix D explains hardware standardization behind revised timing measurements. These substantially expand practical documentation, although conflicting split counts remain unresolved. Code and dataset-license access information is retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds positioning against test-time adaptation and Reed et al.'s sequential self-supervised pre-training, alongside Goyal and Tsai citations, and removes the Mixtral reference. Core GFM/GDA and UDA positioning remains. Publication updates for existing references do not represent additional cited works.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites in the introduction, related work, experimental discussion, and conclusion. Broader Impact becomes Impact Statement; MAE/DinoV2 training paragraphs are reordered, and dataset information and licensing are consolidated. The overall section sequence and method narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reworked: Table 1 becomes full-width, numerous tables gain timing columns and row numbers, and tables are resized and redistributed. A new dataset Table 18 is added, moving the unchanged emissions table to Table 19. Figure 7 uses a tighter accuracy range, while Figures 3–6 receive legend edits.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the efficiency claims easier to assess through broader compute reporting, additional controls, and MAE results that include a negative GlobalWheat outcome. It also better acknowledges relevant prior work. The gain is limited by inconsistencies in the new documentation, particularly Table 18's split counts versus Section 6.1.4. Since v3 already contained strong experimental and compute analyses, these additions support a modest overall improvement.
